subject: cold shower
title: What If You Took a Cold Shower Every Day?

scenes.text: What if you ended every shower ice cold? One big study found a strange result.
The first seconds trigger cold shock: an involuntary gasp, and your heart rate and blood pressure jump. It passes in under a minute.
In 2015, more than 3,000 Dutch adults finished their showers with 30, 60 or 90 seconds of cold, for a month.
They took 29 percent fewer sick days off work.
But they got ill just as often. They simply felt able to go to work anyway. And 30 seconds worked as well as 90.
A 2025 review of 11 studies found the stress drop lasted only about 12 hours. The cold doesn't stop colds. It changes how you cope.

description:
What if you took a cold shower every day? In a 2016 PLOS ONE trial, 3,018 Dutch adults ended hot showers with 30, 60 or 90 seconds of cold for 30 days. Sickness absence fell 29%, but the number of illness days did not change.
A 2025 review of 11 studies found lower stress for about 12 hours and very little evidence for mood or immunity boosts. Sudden cold water triggers a gasp reflex and spikes heart rate and blood pressure.
